([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]) | college = | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = Team Elite | years2 = 2022–present | team2 = City Reapers | highlights = * 2× [[Overtime Elite|OTE]] champion (2022, 2023) * 2× OTE Finals MVP (2022, 2023) * OTE Most Valuable Player (2023) * All-OTE First Team (2023) }} '''Ausar Thompson''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|s|ɑːr}}; born January 30, 2003){{cite AV media|title=Ausar Thompson Interview - Overtime Elite Practice - 12.5.22 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i6ryvGmBnPI |time=0:09 |publisher=Pro Insight |via=[[YouTube]] |date=2022-12-09 | accessdate=2023-02-17 }} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the City Reapers of [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE). He played basketball for [[Pine Crest School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], where he was rated a five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and won a state title. Thompson bypassed his senior year of high school to sign with OTE, where he played for two seasons. He won two straight OTE titles, earning Finals [[most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) twice, and was named league MVP in 2023. == Early life == Thompson was born to Maya Wilson and Troy Thompson and raised in [[San Leandro, California]].{{cite web |last1=Gutierrez |first1=Israel |title=The Thompson twins and Overtime Elite's unproven path to the NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34487913/the-thompson-twins-elite-unproven-path-nba |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=August 31, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Polacheck |first1=Jacob |title=An Audacious Dream Meets Itself in Reality: A Look Inside Overtime Elite's Inaugural Season |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/04/18/an-audacious-dream-meets-itself-in-reality-a-look-inside-overtime-elites-inaugural-season/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=April 18, 2022}} His identical twin brother, [[Amen Thompson|Amen]], is an NBA prospect, and his older brother, Troy Jr., played [[college basketball]] for [[Prairie View A&M Panthers basketball|Prairie View A&M]]. His uncle, [[Mark Thompson (hurdler)|Mark Thompson]], represented [[Jamaica]] in [[Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Men's 400 metres hurdles|400 meter hurdles]] at the [[1992 Summer Olympics]]. He and Amen began training for basketball under the guidance of their father by age seven and drew inspiration from [[LeBron James]]. The twins were [[Homeschooling|homeschooled]] in sixth and seventh grade to focus on basketball. ==High school career== Entering eighth grade, Thompson and his family moved to [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] so that he and Amen could play high school basketball one year early at [[Pine Crest School]].{{cite web |last1=Schoenfield |first1=Bruce |title=The Teenagers Getting Six Figures to Leave Their High Schools for Basketball |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/30/magazine/overtime-elite-basketball-nba.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=November 30, 2021}} The twins immediately started for the team.{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=David |title='I did not think we were going to win': Pine Crest wins state title with miracle comeback |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/prep-broward/article249715043.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 6, 2021}} As a sophomore, Thompson averaged 17.3 points, 6.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game, earning second-team All-[[Broward County, Florida|County]] honors. Entering his junior season, he was named to the Broward County Fab Five by the ''[[Sun Sentinel]]''.{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=Broward County boys basketball Fab Five for 2020 (and the next five) |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-fab-five-broward-2020-20201215-xchw56365nft5kj73jym3z7uw4-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=December 15, 2020}} Thompson averaged 22.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, helping his team win the Class 4A state championship. He shared Broward County Class 5A-1A co-player of the year with Amen.{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=Broward 5A-1A boys basketball co-players of the year: Ausar Thompson and Amen Thompson, Pine Crest juniors |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-county/fl-sp-ss-prem-ac-br-bhoop-small-poy-20210328-qjyzjbndyndqpksczpjufut46q-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 27, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Thompson was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |title=Ausar Thompson – Basketball Recruiting |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/243381/ausar-thompson |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 18, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Ausar Thompson |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/ausar-thompson-260429?view=pv |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 18, 2023}} He gained interest from college programs in 2019, receiving a scholarship offer from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Justin |title=South Florida's Thompson Twins are catching on with recruiters |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/player/201910/south-floridas-thompson-twins-are-catching-recruiters |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=October 2, 2019}} Following his junior year, Thompson held offers from Alabama, Arizona, Auburn, Arizona State and Kansas, among other programs, before deciding to not play [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Brnaham |first1=Travis |title=Elite twins Amen and Ausar Thompson skip college to join the Overtime Elite program |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Amen-Thompson-Ausar-Thompson-commitment-Overtime-Elite-professional-pro-route-165746766/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=May 25, 2021}} == Professional career == === Team Elite (2021–2022) === On May 25, 2021, Thompson signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in [[Atlanta]] with players between ages 16 and 20. He joined the league with Amen, bypassing his final year of high school and college.{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Overtime Elite lands another set of twins as Amen and Ausar Thompson choose professional program over college |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/overtime-elite-lands-another-set-of-twins-as-amen-and-ausar-thompson-choose-professional-program-over-college/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=May 25, 2021}}{{cite magazine |last1=Woo |first1=Jeremy |title=Can Overtime Elite Disrupt Basketball With ... Twins? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/03/07/overtime-elite-thompson-twins-daily-cover |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 7, 2022}} In the 2021–22 season, Thompson played for Team Elite, one of three teams in the league, and averaged 14.7 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.2 blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Araiza |first1=Robert |title=Amen & Ausar Thompson: Should the San Antonio Spurs roll the dice? |url=https://airalamo.com/posts/amen-ausar-thompson-should-san-antonio-spurs-roll-dice/2 |publisher=Air Alamo |agency=[[FanSided]]|access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023}}{{cite web |last1=Sprung |first1=Shlomo |title=Overtime Elite Roster 2022-23 |url=https://boardroom.tv/overtime-elite-roster-2022-23/ |publisher=Boardroom |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=August 26, 2022}} He competed against other OTE teams, as well as [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] and [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] opponents.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Overtime Elite announces 2021-22 schedule, roster for inaugural season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32381206/over-elite-announces-2021-22-schedule-roster-inaugural-season |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=October 13, 2021}} He led his team to the league championship and was named Finals MVP after recording 20 points and 11 rebounds in a 52–45 win over Team OTE in the decisive third game of the finals.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Team Elite Wins First Overtime Elite Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b82a7362-6679-4e97-be6a-bf55e3294708 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=March 14, 2022}} Thompson played for OTE affiliate Team Overtime in [[The Basketball Tournament 2022|The Basketball Tournament]] in July 2022. His team lost to Omaha Blue Crew, 74–70, in the first round of the tournament.{{cite web |last1=DeMarinis |first1=Matt |title=Omaha Blue Crew outlasts Team Overtime in a battle of old versus new |url=https://whiteandbluereview.com/omaha-blue-crew-outlasts-team-overtime-in-a-battle-of-old-versus-new/ |publisher=White and Blue Review |access-date=January 28, 2021 |date=July 17, 2022}} === City Reapers (2022–present) === In the 2022–23 OTE season, Thompson was named [[Captain (sports)|captain]] of the City Reapers and played alongside Amen.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Roster Reveal and Expansion for Season 2 |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d8ad12ca-acbd-44d1-b6d9-9f5f1c5def45 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=September 21, 2022}} On December 12, 2022, he earned league Player of the Week honors.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Ausar Thompson Named Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d075e871-2cfc-4b16-a41b-f14ceafa559d |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=December 12, 2022}} Thompson was selected as Player of the Week for a second time on February 6, 2023, after posting a league single-game record 12 assists, with 17 points and eight rebounds in 21 minutes against the Holy Rams.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=Ausar Thompson Named OTE Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/6fdd1cc4-30ba-4a40-be5f-33dd9681a473 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=February 6, 2023}} At the end of the regular season, he was named OTE MVP and made the All-OTE First Team, with averages of 16.3 points, 7.1 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 2.4 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Cobb |first1=David |title=2023 NBA Draft: Amen, Ausar Thompson declare as likely lottery picks after playing for Overtime Elite |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2023-nba-draft-amen-ausar-thompson-declare-as-likely-lottery-picks-after-playing-for-overtime-elite/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=April 21, 2023}}{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Regular Season Awards |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b66abb33-0079-4dc0-9858-7f6933f9a54a |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=February 20, 2023}} Thompson led the Reapers to the league title in a 3–0 [[Whitewash (sport)|sweep]] of the YNG Dreamerz, repeating as Finals MVP. In the final game, he made a game-winning three-pointer with three seconds left.{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Joseph |title=City Reapers Win OTE Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/81ad0922-4800-435b-9706-a5a6180ceb56 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=March 7, 2023}} On April 21, 2023, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], where analysts viewed him as a potential top-10 pick. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://overtimeelite.com/players/cbb0c3ec-f9f2-43e6-bb6e-6e4ef5702d92 Overtime Elite profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Thompson, Ausar}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Overtime Elite players]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:People from San Leandro, California]] [[Category:Pine Crest School alumni]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:American twins]] [[Category:Twin sportspeople]]
